analysis.title: GS Credit MarketStrats: Embrace the Vol and Lean on Val-(uations)
key_insights: Last week saw extreme cross-asset realized volatility, with Friday producing some of the largest moves in recent memory and few historical periods showing higher X-asset realized vol.
The author's call to own vol convexity and uncertainty hedges over the prior two weeks paid off as the X-asset implied vol market repriced from complacency.
Credit was relatively well behaved. iTraxx and CDX widened just above half of the SX5E and SPX implied widening using the historical credit/equity beta.
iTraxx Main moved +3.375bps wider on Friday, which is not benign but was modest relative to equities and rates.

European PT channel flows were orderly. EUR IG showed 1.1x client sells vs 1x buys, EUR HY showed 1.7x client buys vs 1x sells, and the sub-financial cash trader reported no one hitting bids and RMs still adding risk.

Rates/credit spread correlation has turned negative, making duration an automatic stabilizer for credit total returns. Both USD IG and EUR IG indices posted positive total returns last week, unlike the mid-August to end-September widening when rates and spreads both widened.
Credit fund flows held up per Lipper, with inflows to EUR IG, EUR HY and USD IG and some outflows from USD HY, providing technical support.
The author keeps a framework of a credit spread squeeze into year-end. Last week's widening reversed the prior week's progress, but a sustained move wider is seen as unlikely.
Supports for the view: spread valuations are back at historical medians, investors are not over-risked, flows are steady, and December is the lowest issuance month seasonally.
Trade idea: buy a Jan iTraxx Main 60 strike receiver vs sell a 70-80 payer spread, for a net premium paid structure with positive MtM if spreads tighten and capped downside if they widen.
Keep sourcing carry through defensive longs such as iTraxx Main 5y5y forward, described as underappreciated, and use the carry to fund SPX/NDX gamma/vol.

Trade idea: long European bank equities (SX7E, which fell 7% last week after a rally in early November) vs owning protection via European Senior Financials CDS. iTraxx SnrFin skew screens wide, so shorting single names is cheaper than the index.

sector_views.rationale: Bank stocks screen as a reasonable source of upside on fundamentals and valuations after a 7% selloff last week.
Valuations at historical median, supportive flows and technicals, low December issuance, and a year-end squeeze framework.

trade_ideas.risk: Max loss unlimited per the disclosure, with capped downside into spread widening as the structure is described.

trade_ideas.description: Long iTraxx Main 5y5y forward as defensive carry, funding long SPX/NDX gamma/vol
trade_ideas.rationale: Carry from the defensive long funds convexity in equity vol.

trade_ideas.description: Long SX7E European bank equities vs long protection on European Senior Financials CDS (single names preferred to index)
trade_ideas.rationale: Banks screen reasonable on fundamentals and valuations, and the SnrFin index skew is wide so single-name shorts are cheaper.

risk_factors: Macro-economic uncertainty is underpriced and cross-asset volatility remains elevated.
Further equity and rates weakness could drag credit spreads wider.
Spread widening in rates and credit together, as in mid-August to end-September, would remove the duration cushion.
Max loss on the structure is described as unlimited.
vol_and_positioning: X-asset realized volatility is near historic highs, and implied vol repriced higher after earlier complacency.
The author favors owning vol convexity and uncertainty hedges, and suggests funding SPX/NDX gamma/vol with carry from iTraxx Main 5y5y forward longs.
iTraxx SnrFin index skew (traded spread minus NAV spread) screens wide, favoring single-name shorts over the index.
Credit investors do not appear over-risked, and PT flows show EUR HY client buying at 1.7x vs sells.

tension_points.bull_case: Valuations are at historical median, investors are not over-risked, flows are holding and December issuance is seasonally lowest, so a year-end squeeze is likely.
tension_points.bear_case: Last week's widening reversed the prior week's progress, and the environment is tricky given high cross-asset volatility and a difficult year for investors.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained move wider in spreads, such as a joint rates and spread selloff like mid-August to end-September.
